CLOSE GATE CAUGHT A REAL RECORDING GAP, and it was right to refuse. The close failed with: 'commit b86a1b4c293 changes src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py, which the recorded file_impact does not declare, so the work went beyond the reviewed plan.'

That is accurate. bridge.py holds the THIRD _positive_int twin. It was found during review remediation and explicitly added to the plan's Scope section - the description says so verbatim, 'Added by review remediation: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py — the THIRD _positive_int twin (bridge.py:17). The census named it but the Scope list omitted it, which would have left the twin unrewired and made AC1's definition-count assertion unsatisfiable.' But the recorded file_impact was never updated to match the corrected Scope, so the two drifted and the gate noticed.

The code is correct and merged: all three twins import the consolidated converter (request.py:15, bridge.py:15, reconcile.py:17), and exactly one argparse 'def _positive_int(value: str) -> int' exists at _cli/_parsers/_common.py:19. Only the RECORD was short.

file_impact is now the full 13 paths. That is an attestation-affecting change, so a re-review is required before the close can proceed. Worth noting the pattern: leaf 1cf6 hit exactly this same failure in this run (its file_impact omitted gc_trigger.py, which its Scope named), so 'Scope was corrected during review but file_impact was not' is a repeatable trap rather than a one-off - the two are edited separately and nothing cross-checks them until the close gate does.
